Verified live: cursor output contains git-branch-cleanup.mdc / git-clean-worktrees.mdc; zero requires_claude_code:true skills leak (the flag mechanism itself works — spot-read grill-me.mdc and plan-builder.mdc contain nothing Claude-Code-specific). issues.description: Archived-skill leak vs the trued-up SR1 claim: skills/archive/{git-branch-cleanup,git-clean-worktrees}/SKILL.md are tracked in git with requires_claude_code: false, and convert.sh's walk has no skills/archive/ exclusion, so every non-Claude-Code host receives 36 artifacts (the 34 claimed catalog skills + 2 deprecated archived ones). Pre-existing on main (same flags there), so not a regression introduced by this diff — but the README's new '34 of the 71 skills today' portability claim is not strictly true of converter output on a clean checkout, and deprecated content ships to ten hosts.
issues.suggested_fix: Either add a skills/archive/ exclusion to convert.sh's SKILL.md walk (mirroring lint-skills.sh's debris skip) or set requires_claude_code: true on both archived skills; then regenerate integrations/ where present.

issues.description: convert.sh also emits gitignored local workspace debris when present (observed: skills/meta/skill-review-workspace/.../deep-explainer converted to cursor output as deep-explainer.mdc). lint-skills.sh gained a gitignored-debris skip in this very diff (bats test 343) but convert.sh did not get the same treatment. Local-machine noise only — CI checkouts never contain the debris.
issues.suggested_fix: Apply the same gitignore-aware skip (or an explicit workspace-dir exclusion list) to convert.sh's file walk.

issues.description: Cache cleanup depends on cooperation: the EXIT trap is registered only when the sourcing script has no EXIT trap of its own, and scripts that later install one (as convert.sh does) must remember to call fm_cache_clear from it. A future script that sets an EXIT trap after sourcing and forgets will silently leak ats-fm-cache.* dirs in TMPDIR. The header documents this; noting it as a maintenance tripwire.
issues.suggested_fix: None required now; consider a lint-hooks-style grep asserting any script that both sources frontmatter.sh and sets 'trap ... EXIT' also references fm_cache_clear.

issues.description: The SR13 version-drift guard (--changed) is deliberately not wired into CI, so it only fires when someone runs it locally (it was run as a gate for this build and passed: 30 changed SKILL.md, 0 drifts). The RV8/SR13 drift pattern it exists to kill was a recurring-miss class; an unwired guard can silently stop being run.
issues.suggested_fix: Follow-up: add a PR-only CI step running scripts/lint-skills.sh --changed origin/main (needs fetch-depth to see the base ref).
